title: Russia completes withdrawal from the CFE treaty and NATO suspends it
body:
On 7 November 2023, Russia's Foreign Ministry said that Moscow had officially withdrawn from the Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe (CFE), completing a process that had lasted years. Russian President Vladimir Putin had signed a bill denouncing the treaty in May 2023. Russia had partially suspended compliance with the treaty in 2007 and had stopped taking part in it in 2015.

The same day, NATO announced that it would suspend the CFE Treaty. NATO's press service called the treaty a cornerstone of Euro-Atlantic security and said that "a situation whereby Allied States Parties abide by the Treaty, while Russia does not, would be unsustainable." NATO allies condemned Russia's withdrawal and its war against Ukraine.

The CFE Treaty was signed in Paris in November 1990 as an arms control agreement, by 16 NATO members and six former Warsaw Pact countries, including the Soviet Union, and took effect two years later. It set limits on categories of conventional weapons in Europe. Five days earlier, on 2 November 2023, Putin had signed a law revoking Russia's ratification of the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, which Russia had signed in 1996 and ratified in 2000.
